prompt: I'm building an Angular 21 dashboard that fetches data from three different REST APIs (users, orders, analytics). I need a robust error handling strategy. For HTTP errors, I want: typed error responses from the backend (the API returns { code: string, message: string, details?: Record<string, string> }), retry logic for transient failures (503, 429), user-facing error messages that distinguish between 'try again' errors and 'contact support' errors, and a global error handler that sends errors to our analytics service. Show me the interceptor, the error handling service, and how a component consumes it. Use httpResource where it makes sense.
assertions: Defines a typed interface for the backend error response (code, message, details)
Uses HttpInterceptorFn or functional interceptor (not class-based HttpInterceptor)
Implements retry logic for specific HTTP status codes (503, 429) using RxJS retry/retryWhen
Distinguishes transient (retryable) errors from permanent errors in the error service
Custom ErrorHandler class extends or implements ErrorHandler and reports to analytics
Component uses httpResource() or resource() for at least one API call
Error states in the component template use resource status/error properties or catchError patterns
Uses provideHttpClient with withInterceptors() in the app config
